```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", out.width = "100%")
```

pedkindraw draws a pedigree in two steps. `makePedigreeMatingLayout()` works
out where each animal and each mating goes, and `drawPedigreeDiagram()` draws
that layout as an interactive picture: in the RStudio viewer, in a web page or
in a document such as this one. This vignette shows what a drawing shows and
how to change it, one feature at a time, on small pedigrees typed in the code.
The last drawing is the 375-animal example pedigree that comes with the
package. In each drawing you can zoom with the mouse wheel or a trackpad, drag
to move the picture, hover over an animal, and pick one in the "Select by id"
box.

```{r helpers, include = FALSE}
## For the hidden checks below, each of which holds what the text around it
## says: the vignette stops building if one no longer holds. Where a node is
## drawn, the repeat nodes of an animal, and the mating dot whose two mate
## lines come from two given nodes.
xOf <- function(layout, id) layout$nodes$x[match(id, layout$nodes$id)]
yOf <- function(layout, id) layout$nodes$y[match(id, layout$nodes$id)]
repeatsOf <- function(layout, id) {
  names(layout$duplicateToReal)[layout$duplicateToReal == id]
}
matingOf <- function(layout, a, b) {
  e <- layout$edges
  dots <- unique(e$to[startsWith(e$to, "__union_")])
  dots[vapply(dots, function(u) setequal(e$from[e$to == u], c(a, b)),
              logical(1L))][1L]
}
animalsOf <- function(layout) {
  layout$nodes[!startsWith(layout$nodes$id, "__"), ]
}
```

## From a data frame to a drawing

A pedigree is a data frame with one row per animal: its `id`, `sire`, `dam`
and `sex`, and the generation number `gen` that `findGeneration()` gives
(`vignette("pedkindraw")` describes the columns). Here A and B are the
parents of C, D and E, and C and F are the parents of G and H.

```{r family}
library(pedkindraw)

fam <- data.frame(
  id   = c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F", "G", "H"),
  sire = c(NA, NA, "A", "A", "A", NA, "C", "C"),
  dam  = c(NA, NA, "B", "B", "B", NA, "F", "F"),
  sex  = c("M", "F", "M", "F", "F", "F", "F", "M")
)
fam$gen <- findGeneration(fam$id, fam$sire, fam$dam)
layout <- makePedigreeMatingLayout(fam)
drawPedigreeDiagram(layout)
```

Each generation is a row: A and B at the top, their offspring C, D and E
below them, and G and H at the bottom. F has no parents in the pedigree, so
she is a founder like A and B, but she is drawn beside her mate C, on his row.
A mating is the small dot between two mates, with lines down to each of their
offspring, drawn at right angles as kinship2 draws them. In each mating here
the sire is drawn left of the dam, and C, D and E are drawn left to right in
the order of their rows.

The layout is a list. Its `nodes` data frame has a row for each animal and
each mating dot, and for each of the invisible points that the lines turn at,
with the node's place: `x`, and `y`, which grows downward. The ids of the
dots and points start with two underscores. Its `edges` data frame has a row
for each line.

```{r layoutNodes}
names(layout)
animals <- layout$nodes[!startsWith(layout$nodes$id, "__"), ]
data.frame(id = animals$id, shape = animals$shape,
           x = round(animals$x), y = animals$y)
```

```{r familyClaims, include = FALSE}
rowOf <- function(id) yOf(layout, id)
stopifnot(
  rowOf("A") == rowOf("B"), rowOf("C") > rowOf("A"),
  rowOf("C") == rowOf("D"), rowOf("D") == rowOf("E"),
  rowOf("G") > rowOf("C"), rowOf("G") == rowOf("H"),
  identical(sort(unique(animals$y)), c(0, 150, 300)),
  fam$gen[fam$id == "F"] == 0L, rowOf("F") == rowOf("C"),
  xOf(layout, "A") < xOf(layout, matingOf(layout, "A", "B")),
  xOf(layout, matingOf(layout, "A", "B")) < xOf(layout, "B"),
  rowOf(matingOf(layout, "A", "B")) == rowOf("A"),
  xOf(layout, "C") < xOf(layout, matingOf(layout, "C", "F")),
  xOf(layout, matingOf(layout, "C", "F")) < xOf(layout, "F"),
  rowOf(matingOf(layout, "C", "F")) == rowOf("C"),
  xOf(layout, "F") < xOf(layout, "D"),
  xOf(layout, "C") < xOf(layout, "D"), xOf(layout, "D") < xOf(layout, "E"),
  xOf(layout, "G") < xOf(layout, "H"),
  any(grepl("^__(bar|drop)_", layout$nodes$id)),
  all(layout$nodes$size[grepl("^__(bar|drop)_", layout$nodes$id)] == 0),
  setequal(animals$id, fam$id),
  all(startsWith(setdiff(layout$nodes$id, fam$id), "__")),
  identical(names(layout), c("nodes", "edges", "duplicateToReal",
                             "isolatedIds", "conditions",
                             "conditionsNotDrawn", "hints"))
)
```

## Symbols and the legend

The symbol shows the sex: a square for `"M"`, a circle for `"F"`, a star for
`"H"` (a hermaphrodite), a triangle for `"U"` (unknown) and a diamond for any
other code or none (`NA`), "Other / Unrecorded" in the legend. An optional
`status` column marks with a slash each animal whose status is `"DECEASED"`.
Here S1 and D1 have one offspring of each sex code, and S1 has died.

```{r symbols}
kids <- data.frame(
  id     = c("S1", "D1", "female", "male", "hermaphrodite", "unknown",
             "unrecorded"),
  sire   = c(NA, NA, "S1", "S1", "S1", "S1", "S1"),
  dam    = c(NA, NA, "D1", "D1", "D1", "D1", "D1"),
  sex    = c("M", "F", "F", "M", "H", "U", NA),
  status = c("DECEASED", "ALIVE", "ALIVE", "ALIVE", "ALIVE", "ALIVE",
             "ALIVE")
)
kids$gen <- findGeneration(kids$id, kids$sire, kids$dam)
kidsLayout <- makePedigreeMatingLayout(kids)
drawPedigreeDiagram(kidsLayout)
```

The legend on the right of every drawing lists the five symbols, then
"Affected" (see Conditions, below) and "Deceased", then the lines: the dashed
line that joins two places of the same animal, and the three twin lines.
Hover over an animal to see its id, sex, generation, sire and dam, and each
condition; hover over a mating dot to see how many offspring it has. While
you hover, the animals and lines that are not near the one under the pointer
turn gray.

```{r symbolsClaims, include = FALSE}
kidsAnimals <- animalsOf(kidsLayout)
kidsDiagram <- drawPedigreeDiagram(kidsLayout)
legendNodes <- kidsDiagram$x$legend$nodes
legendEdges <- kidsDiagram$x$legend$edges
dot <- matingOf(kidsLayout, "S1", "D1")
other <- kids
other$sex[other$id == "unrecorded"] <- "X"
otherLayout <- makePedigreeMatingLayout(other)
stopifnot(
  identical(kidsAnimals$shape[match(c("male", "female", "hermaphrodite",
                                      "unknown", "unrecorded"),
                                    kidsAnimals$id)],
            c("square", "dot", "star", "triangle", "diamond")),
  identical(otherLayout$nodes$shape[otherLayout$nodes$id == "unrecorded"],
            "diamond"),
  identical(kidsAnimals$id[kidsAnimals$deceased], "S1"),
  identical(legendNodes$label,
            c("Female", "Male", "Hermaphrodite", "Unknown",
              "Other / Unrecorded", "Affected", "Deceased")),
  identical(legendNodes$shape[1:5],
            c("dot", "square", "star", "triangle", "diamond")),
  identical(legendEdges$label, c("Same animal, again", "MZ", "DZ", "?")),
  isTRUE(legendEdges$dashes[[1L]]),
  identical(kidsDiagram$x$legend$position, "right"),
  identical(kidsLayout$nodes$title[kidsLayout$nodes$id == "unknown"],
            paste0("<b>ID:</b> unknown<br><b>Sex:</b> Unknown",
                   "<br><b>Generation:</b> 1<br><b>Sire:</b> S1",
                   "<br><b>Dam:</b> D1")),
  identical(kidsLayout$nodes$title[kidsLayout$nodes$id == dot],
            "5 offspring"),
  isTRUE(kidsDiagram$x$highlight$enabled),
  isTRUE(kidsDiagram$x$highlight$hoverNearest)
)
```

## Conditions

A column whose name starts with `affected` is a condition. With one such
column, an animal whose value is `TRUE` (or 1) is filled pink, `FALSE` (or 0)
leaves it white, and `NA` fills it gray, so that an animal whose status is not
known does not look unaffected; the legend then has a gray row "Affected status
unknown". Hovering over an animal says Yes, No or Unknown. Here D and G are
affected, and whether H is affected is not known.

```{r oneCondition}
fam1 <- fam
fam1$affected <- c(FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, NA)
layout1 <- makePedigreeMatingLayout(fam1)
drawPedigreeDiagram(layout1)
```

With two to four condition columns, each symbol is cut into one section per
condition, filled in that condition's color where the animal is affected,
and each condition's row in the legend shows the sections with its own
filled; a section whose status is not known is gray. The sections go
counter-clockwise from the top, in the order of the columns. The column's name
gives the label: `affected_diabetes` becomes "Affected (diabetes)". The drawing
grows 45 pixels taller for each condition past the first, and for the "Affected
status unknown" row, to make room in the legend. Here C has diabetes, B and E
are obese, and A has arthritis; G has diabetes and is obese, and whether H is
obese is not known, so H's obesity section is gray.

```{r threeConditions}
fam3 <- fam
fam3$affected_diabetes  <- c(FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE,
                             FALSE)
fam3$affected_obesity   <- c(FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, TRUE, NA)
fam3$affected_arthritis <- c(TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE,
                             FALSE)
layout3 <- makePedigreeMatingLayout(fam3)
layout3$conditions
drawPedigreeDiagram(layout3)
```

A fifth condition column and any after it are not drawn: the layout names
them in `conditionsNotDrawn`.

```{r fiveConditions}
fam5 <- fam3
fam5$affected_cataract     <- FALSE
fam5$affected_hypertension <- FALSE
layout5 <- makePedigreeMatingLayout(fam5)
layout5$conditions$label
layout5$conditionsNotDrawn
```

```{r conditionsClaims, include = FALSE}
fill1 <- layout1$nodes$color.background[match(fam1$id, layout1$nodes$id)]
title1 <- layout1$nodes$title[match(c("D", "E", "H"), layout1$nodes$id)]
fam01 <- fam1
fam01$affected <- c(0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 1, NA)
sections <- layout3$nodes$affectedSections[match(fam3$id, layout3$nodes$id)]
names(sections) <- fam3$id
legend3 <- drawPedigreeDiagram(layout3)$x$legend$nodes
stopifnot(
  identical(fill1 == "#CC79A7", c(FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE,
                                  TRUE, FALSE)),
  identical(fill1[fill1 != "#CC79A7"], c(rep("#FFFFFF", 5L), "#BEBEBE")),
  identical(fam1$id[fill1 == "#BEBEBE"], "H"),
  identical(makePedigreeMatingLayout(fam01)$nodes, layout1$nodes),
  endsWith(title1[1L], "<b>Affected:</b> Yes"),
  endsWith(title1[2L], "<b>Affected:</b> No"),
  endsWith(title1[3L], "<b>Affected:</b> Unknown"),
  identical(drawPedigreeDiagram(layout1)$x$legend$nodes$label[6:7],
            c("Affected", "Affected status unknown")),
  identical(layout3$conditions$label,
            c("Affected (diabetes)", "Affected (obesity)",
              "Affected (arthritis)")),
  identical(unname(sections[c("A", "B", "C", "E", "G", "H")]),
            c("001", "010", "100", "010", "110", "0?0")),
  all(sections[c("D", "F")] == "000"),
  all(animalsOf(layout3)$color.background == "#FFFFFF"),
  grepl("<b>Affected \\(obesity\\):</b> Unknown",
        layout3$nodes$title[layout3$nodes$id == "H"]),
  identical(legend3$label[6:8], layout3$conditions$label),
  identical(legend3$shape[6:8], rep("image", 3L)),
  identical(legend3$label[9L], "Affected status unknown"),
  identical(legend3[["color.background"]][9L], "#BEBEBE"),
  identical(drawPedigreeDiagram(layout)$height, "500px"),
  identical(drawPedigreeDiagram(layout1)$height, "545px"),
  identical(drawPedigreeDiagram(layout3)$height, "635px"),
  nrow(layout5$conditions) == 4L,
  identical(layout5$conditionsNotDrawn, "affected_hypertension")
)
```

## Twins

Twins are listed in a table of their own, one pair per row: `id1`, `id2` and
`code`, which is `"MZ twin"`, `"DZ twin"` or `"UZ twin"` (identical,
fraternal or unknown). `checkTwinRelations()` stops if a pair is not
possible: MZ and DZ twins must have the same sire and dam, and MZ twins the
same sex. The layout takes the table as `twinRelations` and draws a green
line between the two animals of each pair: solid and labeled "MZ", dashed
and labeled "DZ", or with long dashes and labeled "?".

```{r twins}
litter <- data.frame(
  id   = c("S1", "D1", "A1", "A2", "B1", "B2", "C1", "C2"),
  sire = c(NA, NA, "S1", "S1", "S1", "S1", "S1", "S1"),
  dam  = c(NA, NA, "D1", "D1", "D1", "D1", "D1", "D1"),
  sex  = c("M", "F", "F", "F", "M", "F", "M", "M")
)
litter$gen <- findGeneration(litter$id, litter$sire, litter$dam)
twins <- data.frame(
  id1  = c("A1", "B1", "C1"),
  id2  = c("A2", "B2", "C2"),
  code = c("MZ twin", "DZ twin", "UZ twin")
)
twins <- checkTwinRelations(litter, twins)
twinLayout <- makePedigreeMatingLayout(litter, twinRelations = twins)
drawPedigreeDiagram(twinLayout)
```

```{r twinsClaims, include = FALSE}
twinEdges <- twinLayout$edges[!is.na(twinLayout$edges$label), ]
stops <- function(pair) {
  inherits(try(checkTwinRelations(litter, pair), silent = TRUE),
           "try-error")
}
stopifnot(
  identical(twinEdges$from, c("A1", "B1", "C1")),
  identical(twinEdges$to, c("A2", "B2", "C2")),
  identical(twinEdges$label, c("MZ", "DZ", "?")),
  all(twinEdges$color == "#009E73"),
  identical(twinEdges$dashes, list(FALSE, c(4L, 4L), c(14L, 8L))),
  all(yOf(twinLayout, twins$id1) == yOf(twinLayout, twins$id2)),
  stops(data.frame(id1 = "B1", id2 = "B2", code = "MZ twin")),
  stops(data.frame(id1 = "S1", id2 = "D1", code = "DZ twin")),
  !stops(data.frame(id1 = "S1", id2 = "D1", code = "UZ twin"))
)
```

## Animals drawn twice

An animal is drawn in its own row under its sire and dam. When it mates with
an animal that also has parents in the pedigree, one of the two is drawn a
second time, beside the other, and a dashed line joins its two places. Here C,
an offspring of A and B, and R, an offspring of P and Q, are the parents of S
and T.

```{r drawnTwice}
two <- data.frame(
  id   = c("A", "B", "C", "P", "Q", "R", "S", "T"),
  sire = c(NA, NA, "A", NA, NA, "P", "C", "C"),
  dam  = c(NA, NA, "B", NA, NA, "Q", "R", "R"),
  sex  = c("M", "F", "M", "M", "F", "F", "F", "M")
)
two$gen <- findGeneration(two$id, two$sire, two$dam)
twoLayout <- makePedigreeMatingLayout(two)
twoLayout$duplicateToReal
drawPedigreeDiagram(twoLayout)
```

R is drawn under her parents P and Q, and again beside her mate C, where S
and T are drawn under their mating. The layout's `duplicateToReal` names each
repeat node and the animal it stands for, and hovering over a repeat says
"(duplicate occurrence)".

```{r drawnTwiceClaims, include = FALSE}
rRepeat <- repeatsOf(twoLayout, "R")
crDot <- matingOf(twoLayout, "C", rRepeat)
dashedTwo <- twoLayout$edges[vapply(twoLayout$edges$dashes, isTRUE,
                                    logical(1L)), ]
stopifnot(
  identical(unname(twoLayout$duplicateToReal), "R"), length(rRepeat) == 1L,
  yOf(twoLayout, "R") == yOf(twoLayout, "C"),
  abs(xOf(twoLayout, "R") - xOf(twoLayout, matingOf(twoLayout, "P", "Q"))) <
    1e-6,
  yOf(twoLayout, rRepeat) == yOf(twoLayout, "C"),
  !is.na(crDot),
  xOf(twoLayout, "C") < xOf(twoLayout, crDot),
  xOf(twoLayout, crDot) < xOf(twoLayout, rRepeat),
  nrow(dashedTwo) == 1L,
  setequal(c(dashedTwo$from, dashedTwo$to), c("R", rRepeat)),
  endsWith(twoLayout$nodes$title[twoLayout$nodes$id == rRepeat],
           "<br><i>(duplicate occurrence)</i>"),
  yOf(twoLayout, "S") > yOf(twoLayout, crDot),
  xOf(twoLayout, "S") < xOf(twoLayout, crDot),
  xOf(twoLayout, crDot) < xOf(twoLayout, "T")
)
```

## Matings of relatives

When a sire and dam are related, that is when their kinship coefficient is
above 0, the two lines from them to their mating are drawn thick and orange;
kinship2 draws a double line. Here C and D are full siblings, with a kinship
coefficient of 0.25, so D is drawn again beside C.

```{r relatives}
sibs <- data.frame(
  id   = c("A", "B", "C", "D", "K"),
  sire = c(NA, NA, "A", "A", "C"),
  dam  = c(NA, NA, "B", "B", "D"),
  sex  = c("M", "F", "M", "F", "F")
)
sibs$gen <- findGeneration(sibs$id, sibs$sire, sibs$dam)
sibsLayout <- makePedigreeMatingLayout(sibs)
drawPedigreeDiagram(sibsLayout)
```

```{r relativesClaims, include = FALSE}
dRepeat <- repeatsOf(sibsLayout, "D")
cdDot <- matingOf(sibsLayout, "C", dRepeat)
orange <- sibsLayout$edges[sibsLayout$edges$color %in% "#D55E00", ]
kSibs <- kinship(sibs$id, sibs$sire, sibs$dam, sibs$gen)
stopifnot(
  kSibs["C", "D"] == 0.25, length(dRepeat) == 1L,
  yOf(sibsLayout, dRepeat) == yOf(sibsLayout, "C"),
  !is.na(cdDot), nrow(orange) == 2L,
  setequal(orange$from, c("C", dRepeat)), all(orange$to == cdDot),
  all(orange$width == 4),
  !any(layout$edges$color %in% "#D55E00")
)
```

## Two edge styles

`edgeStyle = "direct"` draws a straight line from each parent to the mating
dot and from the dot to each offspring, instead of lines at right angles. The
animals and the dots stay where they were. Give `drawPedigreeDiagram()` the
same `edgeStyle`: it sets how far the highlight reaches when you hover.

```{r direct}
direct <- makePedigreeMatingLayout(fam, edgeStyle = "direct")
drawPedigreeDiagram(direct, edgeStyle = "direct")
```

```{r directClaims, include = FALSE}
keep <- !startsWith(layout$nodes$id, "__") |
  startsWith(layout$nodes$id, "__union_")
same <- match(layout$nodes$id[keep], direct$nodes$id)
stopifnot(
  !anyNA(same),
  isTRUE(all.equal(direct$nodes$x[same], layout$nodes$x[keep])),
  all(direct$nodes$y[same] == layout$nodes$y[keep]),
  !any(grepl("^__(bar|drop|proj|jog)_", direct$nodes$id)),
  all(xor(startsWith(direct$edges$from, "__union_"),
          startsWith(direct$edges$to, "__union_"))),
  drawPedigreeDiagram(direct, edgeStyle = "direct")$x$highlight$degree <
    drawPedigreeDiagram(layout)$x$highlight$degree
)
```

## Animals with no relative

An animal with no known parent, no offspring and no twin has nothing to join
it to the others, so the layout leaves it out, says so in a message, and
lists it in `isolatedIds`.

```{r isolated}
withZ <- rbind(fam, data.frame(id = "Z", sire = NA, dam = NA, sex = "M",
                               gen = 0L))
zLayout <- makePedigreeMatingLayout(withZ)
zLayout$isolatedIds
```

```{r isolatedClaims, include = FALSE}
stopifnot(
  identical(zLayout$isolatedIds, "Z"), !"Z" %in% zLayout$nodes$id,
  identical(zLayout$nodes, layout$nodes)
)
```

Two animals that have mated but have no offspring together are not left
out when the `matings` argument names them, one row per mating with its
`sire` and `dam`: they are drawn side by side on one row, joined at a mating
dot with no line down, as kinship2 and Pedixplorer draw a declared mating.
The dot's hover text reads "0 offspring". Here Y is Z's mate.

```{r declared}
withYZ <- rbind(withZ, data.frame(id = "Y", sire = NA, dam = NA, sex = "F",
                                  gen = 0L))
yzLayout <- makePedigreeMatingLayout(
  withYZ, matings = data.frame(sire = "Z", dam = "Y")
)
drawPedigreeDiagram(yzLayout)
```

```{r declaredClaims, include = FALSE}
yzNodes <- yzLayout$nodes
yzDot <- yzNodes$id[which(yzNodes$title == "0 offspring")]
yzAt <- function(id) yzNodes[match(id, yzNodes$id), c("x", "y")]
stopifnot(
  length(yzLayout$isolatedIds) == 0L, length(yzDot) == 1L,
  yzAt("Z")$y == yzAt(yzDot)$y, yzAt("Y")$y == yzAt(yzDot)$y,
  yzAt(yzDot)$x > min(yzAt("Z")$x, yzAt("Y")$x),
  yzAt(yzDot)$x < max(yzAt("Z")$x, yzAt("Y")$x),
  !any(yzLayout$edges$from == yzDot)
)
```

## Layout hints

The layout chooses the order of siblings and of families, and, for two
animals with parents of their own, which one their offspring are drawn
under. Layout hints change these choices. `hints` is a list with `order`,
`mate` or both, in the form kinship2 and Pedixplorer give them.

`order` is a number for each animal, named by its id. Siblings, separate
families and founder couples are drawn left to right in increasing order of
their numbers; an animal without a number keeps its row's place. Here E, D
and C are drawn in that order, and C's mate F and their offspring move with
him.

```{r order}
orderLayout <- makePedigreeMatingLayout(
  fam, hints = list(order = c(C = 3, D = 2, E = 1))
)
drawPedigreeDiagram(orderLayout)
```

`mate` is a data frame with one row per mating to place. `left` and `right`
are its two animals, `left` drawn left of `right`, and `anchor` names the one
under whose own place their offspring are drawn: `"left"`, `"right"`, or
`"either"` for the layout's own choice. Here the anchor is R, so C, not R, is
drawn twice, and S and T are drawn under R's place.

```{r mate}
mateLayout <- makePedigreeMatingLayout(
  two,
  hints = list(mate = data.frame(left = "C", right = "R", anchor = "right"))
)
drawPedigreeDiagram(mateLayout)
```

```{r hintsClaims, include = FALSE}
eitherLayout <- makePedigreeMatingLayout(two, hints = list(mate = data.frame(
  left = "C", right = "R", anchor = "either"
)))
cRepeat <- repeatsOf(mateLayout, "C")
rcDot <- matingOf(mateLayout, cRepeat, "R")
stopifnot(
  xOf(orderLayout, "E") < xOf(orderLayout, "D"),
  xOf(orderLayout, "D") < xOf(orderLayout, "C"),
  xOf(orderLayout, "C") < xOf(orderLayout, "F"),
  xOf(orderLayout, "G") > xOf(orderLayout, "D"),
  xOf(orderLayout, "H") > xOf(orderLayout, "D"),
  identical(unname(mateLayout$duplicateToReal), "C"),
  length(cRepeat) == 1L, !is.na(rcDot),
  yOf(mateLayout, "R") == yOf(mateLayout, "C"),
  xOf(mateLayout, cRepeat) < xOf(mateLayout, rcDot),
  xOf(mateLayout, rcDot) < xOf(mateLayout, "R"),
  abs(xOf(mateLayout, "R") - xOf(mateLayout, matingOf(mateLayout, "P",
                                                      "Q"))) < 1e-6,
  xOf(mateLayout, "S") < xOf(mateLayout, rcDot),
  xOf(mateLayout, rcDot) < xOf(mateLayout, "T"),
  identical(eitherLayout$nodes, twoLayout$nodes),
  identical(eitherLayout$edges, twoLayout$edges)
)
```

The layout returns the hints it used as `hints`, in the same form, so an
edit can start from the layout's own choices; passed back, they give the same
layout. `order` numbers each animal that has a parent by its row (a founder
gets a number only where an order named it, since naming one turns off the
layout's own order of founder lines). `mate` has the rows given, then a row
for each other mating as drawn, except the matings of an animal with three or
more of them, where a row can move its mates.

```{r ownHints}
layout$hints
identical(makePedigreeMatingLayout(fam, hints = layout$hints), layout)
```

```{r ownHintsClaims, include = FALSE}
stopifnot(
  identical(layout$hints$order, c(C = 3, D = 4, E = 5, G = 7, H = 8)),
  identical(layout$hints$mate,
            data.frame(left = c("A", "C"), right = c("B", "F"),
                       anchor = "left")),
  identical(makePedigreeMatingLayout(fam, hints = layout$hints), layout)
)
```

## kinship2 and Pedixplorer objects

`asPedFrame()` converts a kinship2 `pedigree` or a Pedixplorer `Pedigree` to
the data frame, the twins table, the hints and the declared matings that the
layout takes; the matings, from kinship2's relation code 4 or Pedixplorer's
"Spouse" rows, are passed with `matings = x$matings`. kinship2
keeps hints in the object's `hints` element: `order`, and `spouse`, a matrix
with a row for each mating to place, holding the places (row numbers) of its
left and right animal and the anchor, 1 for left, 2 for right and 0 for
either. Here they are set by hand to show their form; `kinship2::autohint()`
makes them for kinship2's own layout, and gives these same hints for this
pedigree. Add the generations before the layout. The chunks below run only
when kinship2 or Pedixplorer is installed.

```{r kinship2, eval = requireNamespace("kinship2", quietly = TRUE)}
p <- kinship2::pedigree(
  id = two$id, dadid = two$sire, momid = two$dam,
  sex = ifelse(two$sex == "M", "male", "female")
)
p$hints <- list(order = 1:8, spouse = matrix(c(3, 6, 2), ncol = 3))
x <- asPedFrame(p)
x$hints
x$ped$gen <- findGeneration(x$ped$id, x$ped$sire, x$ped$dam)
k2Layout <- makePedigreeMatingLayout(x$ped, hints = x$hints)
identical(k2Layout$nodes, mateLayout$nodes)
```

The layout is the one drawn above for the mate hint. Pedixplorer keeps the
same hints as `horder`, already named by id, and `spouse`, a data frame of
`idl`, `idr` and `anchor`:

```{r Pedixplorer, eval = requireNamespace("Pedixplorer", quietly = TRUE)}
px <- Pedixplorer::Pedigree(
  data.frame(id = two$id, dadid = two$sire, momid = two$dam,
             sex = ifelse(two$sex == "M", "male", "female")),
  hints = list(horder = setNames(1:8, two$id),
               spouse = data.frame(idl = "C", idr = "R", anchor = 2))
)
y <- asPedFrame(px)
y$hints
```

Both packages' automatic hints are made for their own layouts, and some of
their mate rows are ones the layout refuses; `asPedFrame()` fixes those, and
a message names each change.

```{r kinship2Claims, include = FALSE, eval = requireNamespace("kinship2", quietly = TRUE)}
pAuto <- p
pAuto$hints <- kinship2::autohint(p)
stopifnot(
  identical(k2Layout$nodes, mateLayout$nodes),
  identical(k2Layout$edges, mateLayout$edges),
  identical(x$ped[, c("id", "sire", "dam", "sex")],
            two[, c("id", "sire", "dam", "sex")]),
  identical(x$hints$mate, data.frame(left = "C", right = "R",
                                     anchor = "right")),
  isTRUE(all.equal(asPedFrame(pAuto)$hints, x$hints))
)
```

```{r PedixplorerClaims, include = FALSE, eval = requireNamespace("Pedixplorer", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("kinship2", quietly = TRUE)}
stopifnot(
  identical(y$hints, x$hints),
  identical(y$ped[, c("id", "sire", "dam", "sex")],
            x$ped[, c("id", "sire", "dam", "sex")])
)
```

## Saving a drawing

A drawing is an htmlwidget, so `htmlwidgets::saveWidget()` saves it as a web
page that any browser opens, with its sections and slashes. The
"Export Diagram (PNG)" button at the bottom right of each drawing saves a
picture of the drawing as you see it, as `pedigree_diagram.png`.

```{r save, eval = FALSE}
diagram <- drawPedigreeDiagram(layout)
htmlwidgets::saveWidget(diagram, "pedigree.html")
```

From a script, `savePedigreeDiagram()` writes the drawing as an SVG, a PDF or a
PNG file, as the file's ending says. `width` and `height` are the page in
inches, and `dpi`, 300 unless you say, is the PNG's pixels per inch of that
page. A headless Chrome (the chromote package, and Chrome or Chromium on the
computer) runs the same drawing the widget shows, so every mark, color and
legend row comes out as drawn, and every id as text. The chunk below starts
Chrome, so it runs only when you run it yourself, not when this vignette is
built.

```{r saveFiles, eval = interactive()}
savePedigreeDiagram(diagram, "pedigree.svg", width = 10, height = 6)
savePedigreeDiagram(diagram, "pedigree.pdf", width = 10, height = 6)
savePedigreeDiagram(diagram, "pedigree.png", width = 10, height = 6, dpi = 150)
```

```{r saveFileClaims, include = FALSE}
## What needs no browser: the arguments the text names and dpi's default.
stopifnot(
  identical(names(formals(savePedigreeDiagram)),
            c("diagram", "file", "width", "height", "dpi")),
  identical(formals(savePedigreeDiagram)$dpi, 300)
)
```

```{r saveClaims, include = FALSE}
exportOptions <- drawPedigreeDiagram(layout)$x$export
stopifnot(
  identical(exportOptions$type, "png"),
  identical(exportOptions$name, "pedigree_diagram.png"),
  identical(exportOptions$label, "Export Diagram (PNG)")
)
```

## Clicks in a Shiny application

A click on a drawing does nothing unless `onClick` gives a JavaScript function
to run. In a Shiny application it can send the id of the node clicked to the
server. The drawing needs 500 pixels of height, 45 more for each condition
past the first.

`runPedigreeApp()` starts such an application, ready made: it draws a
pedigree file, and a click on an animal, or on a repeat of it, makes it the
focal animal, the one whose ancestors and descendants or near relatives the
app can draw. To write your own, the code below sends the id clicked to the
server.

```{r shiny, eval = FALSE}
## In the user interface:
visNetwork::visNetworkOutput("pedigree", height = "500px")

## In the server function:
output$pedigree <- visNetwork::renderVisNetwork({
  drawPedigreeDiagram(layout, onClick = paste(
    "function(params) {",
    "Shiny.setInputValue('pedigreeClick', params.nodes);",
    "}"
  ))
})
shiny::observeEvent(input$pedigreeClick, {
  print(input$pedigreeClick)
})
```

`params.nodes` holds the id of the node clicked: an animal's id, a repeat
node's, which `duplicateToReal` turns into its animal's, or a mating dot's,
which starts with `__union_`.

```{r shinyClaims, include = FALSE}
clickCode <- paste("function(params) {",
                   "Shiny.setInputValue('pedigreeClick', params.nodes);",
                   "}")
stopifnot(
  is.null(drawPedigreeDiagram(layout)$x$events$click),
  identical(as.character(drawPedigreeDiagram(layout, onClick = clickCode)
                         $x$events$click), clickCode)
)
```

## A colony-size drawing

The example pedigree that comes with the package (`vignette("pedkindraw")`)
has 375 rhesus macaques in nine generations, and three twin pairs.

```{r colony}
pedFile <- system.file("extdata", "obfuscated_rhesus_mhc_ped.csv",
                       package = "pedkindraw")
twinFile <- system.file("extdata", "obfuscated_rhesus_mhc_twin_relations.csv",
                        package = "pedkindraw")
ped <- read.csv(pedFile, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
colonyTwins <- read.csv(twinFile, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
ped$gen <- findGeneration(ped$id, ped$sire, ped$dam)
colony <- makePedigreeMatingLayout(ped, twinRelations = colonyTwins)
drawPedigreeDiagram(colony)
```

The warning says that in 72 places a line may pass close to an animal it
does not belong to: in the right-angle style the layout steps a line around
an animal in its way, and these it could not fully clear. Nothing is missing
from the drawing; all 375 animals are in it.

Fitted to the page, the drawing is too small to read its ids. Zoom in to read
them, or pick an animal in the "Select by id" box: the animals and lines that
are not near it turn gray, which shows where it is. The arcs are the dashed
lines that join each of the 113 animals drawn more than once to its other
places.

`savePedigreeDiagram()` writes the whole colony on one page with every id
written: 545 id labels, 375 distinct (the other 170 are the repeat appearances
of those 113 animals), and none overlapping another label. On a 14 by 7 inch
page, the shape the layout fits, or on letter paper (8.5 by 11 inches), an id
is under 1 point high, so in the SVG or the PDF you zoom in to read one. In a
PNG at the default 300 dpi an id is about 3 pixels high, and a larger `dpi`
makes it bigger. As above, the chunk runs only when you run it yourself.

```{r colonyFiles, eval = interactive()}
diagram <- drawPedigreeDiagram(colony)
savePedigreeDiagram(diagram, "colony.pdf", width = 14, height = 7)
savePedigreeDiagram(diagram, "colony.svg", width = 14, height = 7)
savePedigreeDiagram(diagram, "colony.png", width = 14, height = 7)
```

```{r colonyClaims, include = FALSE}
colonyWarning <- NULL
colonyAgain <- withCallingHandlers(
  makePedigreeMatingLayout(ped, twinRelations = colonyTwins),
  warning = function(w) {
    colonyWarning <<- conditionMessage(w)
    invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
  }
)
dashedColony <- colonyAgain$edges[vapply(colonyAgain$edges$dashes, isTRUE,
                                         logical(1L)), ]
colonyDiagram <- drawPedigreeDiagram(colonyAgain)
stopifnot(
  nrow(ped) == 375L, length(unique(ped$gen)) == 9L,
  nrow(colonyTwins) == 3L,
  length(colonyWarning) == 1L,
  startsWith(colonyWarning, paste0("makePedigreeMatingLayout(): 72 ",
                                   "same-row edge-node collision(s)")),
  setequal(animalsOf(colonyAgain)$id, ped$id),
  length(colonyAgain$isolatedIds) == 0L,
  length(unique(colonyAgain$duplicateToReal)) == 113L,
  ## The ids written: each animal once and each repeat appearance (545).
  length(colonyAgain$duplicateToReal) == 170L,
  sum(colonyAgain$nodes$id %in% ped$id) + length(colonyAgain$duplicateToReal) ==
    545L,
  nrow(dashedColony) == length(colonyAgain$duplicateToReal),
  all(dashedColony$smooth.enabled),
  isTRUE(colonyDiagram$x$idselection$enabled)
)
```

## How large a drawing can be

Most of the time a drawing takes goes to the layout, in R. In measurements
made in November 2026 on one Mac (Apple M2 Max), pedkindraw drew pedigrees of
501 to 2,000 animals, taken from nprcgenekeepr's example pedigree of 3,694, in
2.0 seconds for 501 animals, 9.1 seconds for 1,001, 23.5 seconds for 1,500 and
50.5 seconds for 2,000, in R; showing a drawing in Chrome added under a second.
The shape of a pedigree matters as much as its size: two other pedigrees of
about 1,000 animals, made of the ancestors of the last three generations
only, took 16.7 and 19.1 seconds. `runPedigreeApp()` asks before it draws
more than 1,000 animals. In nprcgenekeepr's drawing, from which pedkindraw's
is copied, an animal could still be found by its id at 1,000 animals, and its
lines followed to its parents, once zoomed in.
`vignette("speed", package = "pedkindraw")` times pedkindraw's drawing on
synthetic colonies of 300 to 3,000 animals, beside kinship2's and
Pedixplorer's drawings, with the saved SVG, PDF and PNG files and the memory
each used; judged from those pages, pedkindraw's own drawing can be read up
to 1,000 animals, zoomed in, as nprcgenekeepr's could.

## Where next

The help pages of `makePedigreeMatingLayout()` and `drawPedigreeDiagram()`
give every argument, among them `kinshipMatrix`, which passes the layout
kinship coefficients you have computed; `?asPedFrame` gives each conversion,
and `vignette("pedkindraw")` the rest of the package.
`vignette("speed", package = "pedkindraw")` gives how long a drawing and each
computation take, by the number of animals.
